surfaces.part: snow lip at top of cliff

answer.evidence: The object is a 16px-wide, 64-row vertical cliff face. Rows 1-3 are a white snow strip, which is a 2-3 row rim with no front-edge line or eave shadow and no widening or narrowing. Below it, rows 3-41 are grey rock with dark crack lines, and rows 42-63 are green foliage or water. The silhouette is a constant 16 wide on every row, so there is no ellipse, no roof or canopy, and no visible contents. The whole drawing is a flat vertical face with only a thin snow rim at the top, so it reads as front elevation. It does not read as a gate, pavilion or building.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow, tile-sized strip of grey rock with a dark green patch at the bottom. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. The references are full houses with scalloped tile roofs, half-timber or stone walls, and doors. The candidate shows 9 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, which is comparable. Its dark edge pixels are 86% near-neutral, against 7-9% for the references. That means its outline is a neutral black/grey line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material, which is the sticker look. Its rock ramp has only about 3 distinct lightness steps against roughly 6 on the references. Texture is some, but the stones are not shaded individually the way the reference stones are.
